auditor: muse-spark-1.3 (Meta Model API), one call per section, reasoning_effort low
scope: compiled facts vs the handbook pages they cite (card backs are byte copies of these facts); exam items and lesson narration not checked in this pass

flagged.issue: Page requires 26,001 or more and more than 16 persons including driver, not above 26,001 and 16-plus.
flagged.suggested_fix: Class A is 26,001 or more with towed over 10,000, Class B is 26,001 or more towing 10,000 or less, Class C is under 26,001 placarded hazmat or designed for more than 16 including driver.

flagged.issue: Page 9 does not state the camper and 150-mile farm exemptions, which appear on page 10.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 9, CDL applies to volunteers including church and school bus drivers and exempts non-commerce cars, military and emergency rescue vehicles; camper and 150-mile farm exemptions are on the next page.

flagged.issue: Page bans limited-access highways where minimum speed exceeds 30 mph, not all highways posted above 30 mph.
flagged.suggested_fix: Mopeds cannot be operated on limited-access highways where the minimum speed is more than 30 miles per hour, with headlight/space cushion use and helmets strongly recommended but not required.

flagged.issue: Page allows midnight to 6 a.m. driving on good-cause showing, which the fact omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: Permit holders under 18 may not drive midnight to 6 a.m. unless they can demonstrate good cause, with 180-day hold, 60 hours including 10 at night, adult 21-plus supervision and one unrelated under-20 passenger.

flagged.issue: Page permits intermediate midnight driving for good cause such as emergencies, school or work, omitted by fact.
flagged.suggested_fix: After passing, an Intermediate sticker issues; full license after 180 days plus driver education at 17, with no 12-6 driving unless good cause such as emergency, school or work.

flagged.issue: Page 22 does not state the expired over one year or lost-license testing and clearance rules.
flagged.suggested_fix: New residents must license within 30 days and file residency, legal presence, Social Security and old license; out-of-state permit holders must transfer to a Kentucky permit first at 15-plus.

flagged.issue: Page 25 alone does not state the two-year subsequent accumulation penalty, continued on page 26.
flagged.suggested_fix: Drivers start at no points, face possible suspension at 12 points or 7 under 18 in two years after hearing, points expire in two years with five-year records, and failure to appear draws six months for the first accumulation.

flagged.issue: Page 22 states the college-student rule but not the 30-day new-resident rule.
flagged.suggested_fix: College students may keep a valid home license with a Kentucky school ID in possession; the 30-day new-resident licensing rule is stated on the prior page.

flagged.issue: The 15-day deadline applies only to purchasers and those bringing a vehicle into Kentucky, not to all registration.
flagged.suggested_fix: Before highway operation the owner must register with the county clerk; purchasers and those bringing a vehicle into Kentucky must apply within 15 days, and insurance must be obtained before operation.

flagged.issue: The page says caffeine plus nap gives the benefits of both, not that it doubles the benefit.
flagged.suggested_fix: Try consuming caffeine before a short nap to get the benefits of both, and try not to drive late at night.

flagged.issue: The page does not state the fitting help is free and omits required extreme-indifference and causing-death elements.
flagged.suggested_fix: State the seat should ideally be mid-rear with help at State Police posts, and leaving under-8s is illegal only under extreme indifference creating grave risk thereby causing death.

flagged.issue: Page 40 does not state the cargo-secure definition, which appears on page 39.
flagged.suggested_fix: Remove the cargo clause from this page-40 fact or cite page 39 for the secure-load definition.

flagged.issue: The signal orientation details are on page 42, not on cited page 43.
flagged.suggested_fix: Cite page 42 for red-yellow-green top-to-bottom and horizontal red-left yellow-middle green-right layout.

flagged.issue: The white X stop duty applies only when a train is approaching, which the fact omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: The white X-shaped Railroad Crossing sign requires stopping behind the line only when a train or railroad vehicle is approaching until clear.

flagged.issue: The white X stop duty applies only when a train is approaching, which the contrast omits.
flagged.suggested_fix: The round yellow board warns of tracks ahead, while the white X requires stopping only when a train is approaching.

flagged.issue: Cited page 46 does not state that yellow diamonds warn of danger; that is on page 43.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 46, white regulatory signs state laws to obey and green, brown or blue guides inform; cite page 43 for yellow-diamond warnings.

flagged.issue: Page says slow to "your existing speed" and separately check posted speed, not slow to posted limit.
flagged.suggested_fix: Signal into the deceleration lane and slow to your existing speed, then check the posted speed for the deceleration lane.

flagged.issue: Cited page states the return-mirror and checks but not passing as quickly as possible, which is on another page.
flagged.suggested_fix: To pass: check oncoming, mirrors and shoulder, signal, steer in, continue until complete front is visible in rearview mirror, signal and merge smooth.

flagged.issue: Summary omits that the left lane is also for left-turners on three-or-more-lane roads.
flagged.suggested_fix: Three-or-more lanes use middle for through, left for passing or turning left, and right for slower traffic, while two-lane roads reserve the left for passing.

flagged.issue: The page assigns 500 feet to oncoming vehicles and 300 feet to followed vehicles, not both distances to followers and storms together.
flagged.suggested_fix: Use highs when no oncoming traffic for double reach; use lows when following and in fog, rain or snow, dimming within 500 feet of oncoming vehicles and within 300 feet of followed vehicles.

flagged.issue: Page 77 states the interstate/parkway exception and penalty but does not state the outside city/town/urban-county exception on this page.
flagged.suggested_fix: On page 77, passing is allowed when directed by police or when on an interstate highway or state parkway, with violation punishable by $250 fine or 90 days in jail.

flagged.issue: Page states regulatory signs are white with green and yellow as wrong options but does not state yellow means warning and green means guide.
flagged.suggested_fix: Regulatory signs are white, not green or yellow.

flagged.issue: Page states high beams when no oncoming traffic and lists fog/rain/snow and following as wrong options, but does not state those situations take lows.
flagged.suggested_fix: Use high beams when there is no oncoming traffic approaching, not in fog, rain, snow or when following another vehicle.
